subject: SUBSTITUTE function
notes: CLOSED by kb/Work PB247. Citation re-derived: cite.py --check 15.87.3 'Neither argument-1 nor argument-2 shall be of zero length' -> OK, rule 3. THE RESIDUE WAS A TWO-ARM DISPATCH WITH ONE ARM FIXED: the odd-position argument-2 walk sat BELOW BindSubstitute's 'if (flat)' early return, so the moment any operand was a table(ALL) enumeration the rule went unenforced entirely and FUNCTION SUBSTITUTE(X3 "" "Q" T(ALL)) bound clean although operand[1] was a STATICALLY known zero-length argument-2 - and the mixed written-operand + enumeration shape is real and shipped (2023/pb81_substitute_table_all's MIX line). THE WALK IS NOW ONE PRIVATE METHOD CALLED FROM BOTH EXITS, and it was re-shaped rather than moved: it advances a pair-SLOT counter by each operand's STATIC element count (TableAllPlace.StaticCount, 1 for a written operand) instead of assuming one element per operand, and returns at the first operand whose count is a run-time fact (an OCCURS DEPENDING or DYNAMIC ALL level) - so every operand whose pair role is decidable keeps its compile-time answer, which is strictly more than the old all-or-nothing and makes the next enumeration shape automatic. EVIDENCE, BOTH DIRECTIONS. Rejections: negative/pb247-subst-zero-flat (the flat-path hole itself) and negative/pb247-subst-zero-arg1 (the ARGUMENT-1 half of r3, which no fixture had ever exercised - the two pb58 negatives both target an argument-2), plus the two pb58 negatives, all COBOL1627. Admissions, which matter more because moving the walk above the early return risks over-rejecting: 2023/pb247_substitute_flat_zero_length_arg3 writes a LEGAL zero-length argument-3 before an enumeration - r3 names argument-1 and argument-2 and NOT argument-3 - and FLT=abc proves the slot walk skips the even positions on the flat path; pb58_argument_predicates_legal does the same on the ordinary path. The 15.87.4 r1 run-time twin in CobolIntrinsics.Substitute is unchanged and still answers the genuinely run-time widths.
